reason: Optix's 'External Calendar' webhook events only send a free-text `title` (e.g. 'Jayden Rollinson - 1 Hour Golf Lesson'), not the member.first_name/member_first_name/member_name fields normalizeOptixLessonEvent() looked for. The name parser found nothing, fell back to the 'Optix customer' placeholder, and wrote calendar_items rows directly under that generic label instead of the real customer name. This was not an overwrite of a pre-existing Clarity lesson (external_booking_links has no link to a non-optix-prefixed calendar_items row) -- the lessons were created wrong from the start by the same bug fixed in commit 562c58e ('Stop Optix from overwriting Clarity lessons').
method: Real names recovered from the untouched raw payload_json.title stored in optix_webhook_events (receipt-only, never mutated by the buggy processor) and written back to calendar_items.client/title.

not_recoverable.note: Optix's own payload title was already 'Optix customer - Swing Analysis'; no real name was ever sent.

not_touched.person_id: Left every row's existing person_id (mostly the generic 'Optix customer' placeholder person e2d64666-d738-4393-9885-2474c5ed42fa) unchanged. Several recovered names (Shaun Kao, Adam King, Brian Fox, Samuel Hale) already have multiple duplicate rows in `people` from an earlier dedup bug (see 2026-07-14_duplicate_person_65f7b016.json); guessing which duplicate to relink risked compounding that mess. Only calendar_items.client/title were restored.
